builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SafeOrchestrate: Runtime Checked Intent-Driven Orchestration for Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: The method replaces unconstrained LLM-to-MCP tool use with a pipeline that derives atomic goals from natural-language intent, generates runtime-checkable LTL-style specifications, grounds them to WoT Thing Description affordances, and verifies candidate actions against SMT-backed safety constraints before execution. The cost is added system complexity and latency: the pipeline requires an LTL generation step, a grounding step, and an SMT solver in the execution loop, plus engineering effort to maintain the specification and constraint models. Failure modes include incorrect or incomplete LTL specifications generated by the LLM, grounding errors when affordances are ambiguous, and SMT models that are over-permissive or over-restrictive, which can respectively admit unsafe actions or block legitimate ones.
rationale: The approach is implementable on constrained infrastructure because it uses an LLM plus an SMT solver rather than model training, and the reliability claim is large and directly relevant to safe tool use; however, the evaluation is limited to simulated environments, so production adoption requires validation on the reader's own tasks and safety constraints.
technique: Runtime-checked intent-driven orchestration with formal guardrails

The cost is added system complexity and latency: the pipeline requires an LTL generation step, a grounding step, and an SMT solver in the execution loop, plus engineering effort to maintain the specification and constraint models. Failure modes include incorrect or incomplete LTL specifications generated by the LLM, grounding errors when affordances are ambiguous, and SMT models that are over-permissive or over-restrictive, which can respectively admit unsafe actions or block legitimate ones.
Maintains 100% required action accuracy and 100% MCP Execution Similarity on all but one task (92%), versus a baseline whose MCP ES falls to 13% on multi-device, event-triggered, and ordered tasks.
